messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: p99 latency SLO breach detected for canary v9 (region: us-west-2). Affected endpoint: /v1/generate-stream. p95=820ms (ok), p99=4.2s (breach). Streaming stall count spike +37% in last 5m. Automated health rule triggered paging.

jamie (oncall): paging in. I’m looking. any obvious recent changes? who rolled v9 canary? :eyes: @vishal?

vishal (runtime): I pushed the v9 canary earlier at 03:12 UTC, 10% traffic. Changes: attention cache prefetch tweak + kernel selector update for newer quantized weights. No infra changes.

maria (sre): confirm p99 spike aligns with the canary ramp. grabbing traces and tail logs. link to quick charts: https://internal.redwood/mon/graphs/2198765432 (short-lived link)

maria (sre): quick stats from the last 10m: requests/s +12%, prefix cache hit rate dropped 18%, stream stalls >3s increased from 0.7% -> 4.8%. Most affected shards: inference-pool-uw2-03.

jamie (oncall): this is customer-impacting? @nina any support hits?

nina (support): we’ve had 3 low-pri customer threads escalate to timeouts in last 15m (IDs: CS-9821, CS-9823, CS-9827). One enterprise customer reported streaming cutouts on long completions. They’re on dedicated infra but route through canary for model variant testing.

jamie (oncall): ok paging L2 and runtime. mitigation plan: 1) reduce canary traffic to 0% 2) if that doesn't normalize, rollback the v9 image 3) open status update for customers. I'll run step 1 now.

jamie (oncall): running: 
```
# scale canary traffic down
redwoodctl rollout traffic-shift --model canary-v9 --region us-west-2 --percent 0
```

deploy-bot: roll command accepted. Traffic for canary-v9 in us-west-2 -> 0% (started). Check back in 20s for propagation. :white_check_mark:

vishal (runtime): while traffic shifts, I’m tailing logs. seeing repeated: 
```
[2026-03-15T03:28:12Z] stream_fail: stalled for 7.8s, kvcache_miss=true, kv_rebuild=true, kernel=matmul_q8
[2026-03-15T03:28:13Z] stream_resume: ok
[2026-03-15T03:29:05Z] stream_fail: stalled for 6.1s, kvcache_miss=true
```
Looks like a regressing cache policy under v9; many requests fall back to full attention compute on the slow code path.

maria (sre): that explains p99 widening with only small TPS change. If the canary is causing KV cache churn, reducing traffic should restore hit rates and SLOs.

jamie (oncall): can we verify post-shift? pulling new metrics...

maria (sre): 30s after shift: p99 dropped to 1.1s, stream stalls down to 0.9%. cache hit rate recovering to baseline. looks good.

nina (support): customer CS-9823 reports fewer errors now. They say streaming resumed ~1m ago. I'll update the threads and ask if they want a follow-up call.

jamie (oncall): good mitigation. Next steps: keep canary at 0% for now, mark v9 for rollback, run a targeted perf test in staging to reproduce cache miss pattern, and schedule postmortem. @vishal can you trigger rollback ticket and diagnostics capture?

vishal (runtime): opening rollback / debugging ticket now. Action items I’m taking: 1) capture KV cache metrics and per-shard histograms 2) run the v9 model locally with traffic replay to reproduce 3) check kernel selector config differences between v8 and v9. Ticket: INT-2198.

jamie (oncall): also need a short status update for the incident channel and status page. I'll draft. Anyone object to marking impact as "partial degraded" for 20m window?

maria (sre): agreed. partial degraded, some streaming requests hit increased latency/timeouts. No data loss.

nina (support): notifying affected customer list. drafting email: "We observed intermittent streaming timeouts for certain completions while testing a new canary model. We have rolled the canary back and streaming latency has normalized. We will follow up with a full investigation."

deploy-bot: rollback action available: 
```
# quick rollback (if we decide to roll image)
redwoodctl rollout rollback --model canary-v9 --to-version v8 --region us-west-2
```

vishal (runtime): I want to reproduce before a rollback, but given customer impact and that traffic is already 0% we can proceed with formal rollback to remove risk. scheduling rollback in 10m unless we see reason to hold.

jamie (oncall): do it. schedule now and notify here when done. also tag postmortem owner. I'll assign to @maria.

deploy-bot: rollback initiated by vishal. Rolling back canary-v9 -> v8 in us-west-2. Progress: 3/3 nodes updated.

deploy-bot: rollback complete. canary-v9 removed, traffic pinned to v8. Validation checks: basic health OK, streaming endpoints responding.

maria (sre): running final checks: p95=780ms, p99=0.95s, stream stalls ~0.6%. All within SLO. Captured traces and flamegraphs saved to INT-2198.

nina (support): customers notified. one enterprise contact requested a post-incident call; scheduled for tomorrow.

jamie (oncall): great work. remaining tasks: capture a minimal repro, root cause writeup, postmortem doc (owner: maria), and fix candidate (either patch v9 kv policy or revert kernel selector change). Please update INT-2198 with timelines. I’m closing paging for now.

maria (sre): I’ll own the postmortem. initial blurb: v9 introduced attention prefetch change that increased KV cache churn under production request patterns, causing fallback to slower compute path and visible tail latency regression for streaming.

vishal (runtime): will push a hotfix branch with conservative cache TTL and run load tests. also adding more defensive metrics around kvcache_miss ratio per shard.

jamie (oncall): thanks everyone. leaving a final note on incident channel and updating runbook with a new checklist for canary traffic ramp + kvcache watch thresholds. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: SLOs recovered after canary withdrawal and rollback. Duration: ~22m. Incident record: INT-2198.
